text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS

- Parliament voted to ban independent deputy Gundars Valdmanis from attending six parliamentary meetings. The move was proposed by speaker Alfreds Chepanis after Valdmanis had repeatedly offended colleagues.
- The prime minister's official car, a Volvo-960, crashed into a lamp post.
- President Guntis Ulmanis met German President Roman Herzog, who expressed confidence that Latvia will meet the criteria for joining the EU.
DIENA
- 50 troops from the Baltic battalion returned home after a two-month mission in Bosnia.
- A Russian foreign ministry spokesman said that the introduction of alien's passports in Latvia violates the convention on the reduction of statelessness.
NEATKARIGA RITA AVIZE
- Zemes Bank granted a loan of three million marks to Latvian Post to improve its technical basis.

- Latvian news agency LETA has totally run aground. Lattelekom has cut its phone links, which made impossible further delivery of information. There is a plan to privatise the agency by involving private capital of 8,000 lats.
- Riga city council is to decide on closing two departments of the sixth clinical hospital.
BIZNES & BALTIJA
- Denmark will allocate funds to assist the Baltics in improving customs work and tax collection.
- Finance Minister Robert Zile speaks about the results of his visit to the EBRD shareholders meeting in London.
SM
- The authorities of the Russian district of Pskov urge Latvia to open a trading centre in the city to improve the sales of Latvian products there.
- Riga will host the first NGO forum at which about 350 organisations will be represented.
DIENAS BIZNESS
- The deficit of the state budget was 1.564 million lats on April 15. The deficit of the social insurance budget at the same time was 3.813 million lats.
- The output of Latvian Balsam, the largest of the country's 20 alcohol producers, rose 10 percent in the first quarter of 1997. This was possible due to an increase in exports.
